title: Social media
subtitle: Social media platforms collect your data to sell to advertisers and other data brokers. Best practice would be to delete your social media accounts, but that's not possible for people for a variety of reasons. This comprehensive guide covers nearly every privacy and security-related setting to help you lock down your accounts.

context.title: What social media platforms actually collect
context.body: Social media companies collect more than just what you post. They track your location, what you look at even when you don't interact with it, who you're connected to, your device hardware, as well as your activity all across the web
context.body2: Completing the Critical items will significantly reduce your exposure even if you keep your accounts

warning.body: Changing your social media settings isn't going to 100% protect your information from being tracked, sold to data brokers, or used in advertising. These steps aren't a replacement for deleting your social media

items.name: Password and security
items.path: Meta Accounts Center → Password and security
items.why: This section helps you enhance your account security

steps.text: Open `Meta Accounts Center` → `Password and security`
Create a strong password: `Change password`
Enable 2FA: `Two-factor authentication`
Create a passkey: `Passkey`
If eligible, turn on Advanced Protection: `Advanced Protection`

sources.label: Meta Accounts Center → Password and security

items.name: Connected experiences
items.path: Meta Accounts Center → Connected experiences
items.why: Controls what information is shared between your Meta accounts

steps.text: Open `Meta Accounts Center` → `Connected experiences`
`Sharing across profiles` → disconnect your accounts
FINISH

items.name: Your information and permissions
items.path: Meta Accounts Center → Your information and permissions
items.why: This section covers information Meta has about you that it shares with third parties, and what third parties have shared with it

steps.text: Open `Meta Accounts Center`
Go to `Your information and permissions` → `Your activity off Meta technologies`
Follow the steps for `Disconnect specific activity`
Next, follow the steps for `Clear previous activity`
Then `Manage future activity` → `Disconnect future activity`
Go back to `App connections` → disconnect all apps
Go back to `Specific ad partners` → disconnect all ad partners

sources.label: Meta Accounts Center → Your information and permissions

items.name: Ad preferences
items.path: Meta Accounts Center → Ad preferences → Manage info
items.why: Controls what information Meta can use to serve personalized ads to you

steps.text: Open `Meta Accounts Center` → `Ad preferences` → `Manage info`
Delete and remove items in `Categories used to reach you`
Then `Activity information from ad partners` → `Review Settings` → choose `No, don't make my ads more relevant by using this information`
Delete and remove all sections in `Categories used to reach you`
Next, `Ads in other apps` → choose `Don't allow us to show you ads in other apps`
Next, `Ads about Meta` → choose `Don't use my activity to show me ads about Meta`
Finally, `Social interactions` → select your account(s) → `Who can see your social interactions alongside ads for this account?` → choose `Only Me`

items.name: Make your profile private
items.path: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Privacy Center
items.why: Making your profile private stops strangers from looking for personal details about you

steps.text: Open `Profile` → `Settings & privacy` → `Privacy Center` → `Common privacy settings` → `Manage audience settings` → `Profile information`
Delete personal information such as your family members, relationship, and current city
Set everything else to `Only me` or `Friends`

sources.label: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Privacy Center

items.name: Make past and future posts private
items.path: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Privacy Center
items.why: Making your account private doesn't retroactively make previous posts private

steps.text: Open `Settings & privacy` → `Privacy Center` → `Common privacy settings` → `Manage audience settings` → `Posts and stories`
Change `Who can see future posts` → `Friends`
Next choose `Limit past posts`
Turn off `Allow comment summaries on your posts`
Turn off `Allow visual search on your posts`
Set `Who can see your stories` → `Friends`

sources.label: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Privacy Center

items.name: Restrict who can find and contact you
items.path: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Settings → How people find and contact you
items.why: By default, anyone can search for your Facebook profile using your phone number or email address. This is one way stalkers and scammers find targets.

steps.text: Open `Settings & privacy` → `Settings` → `How people find and contact you`
Set `Who can send you friend requests` → `Friends of friends`
Set `Who can see your friends list` → `Friends`
Set `Who can Facebook suggest your profile to based on your phone number or email address` → `People with your email address` → `No one`
Set `Who can Facebook suggest your profile to based on your phone number or email address` → `People with your phone number` → `No one`
Turn off `Do you want search engines outside of Facebook to link to your profile?`
Set `For people with your phone number, deliver requests to` → `Message requests` or `Don't receive requests`
Set `For friends of friends on Facebook, deliver requests to` → `Message requests` or `Don't receive requests`
Set `Deliver requests from people in your Facebook groups to` → `Message requests` or `Don't receive requests`
Set `For others on Messenger or Facebook, deliver requests to` → `Message requests` or `Don't receive requests`

sources.label: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Settings → How people find and contact you

items.name: Disable off-Facebook activity
items.path: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Settings → Apps and websites
items.why: Disconnect connections with other apps and websites and disable using Facebook to log into other websites

steps.text: Open `Settings & privacy` → `Settings` → `Apps and websites`
Remove connected apps and websites; be sure to change your login info first
Set `Apps, websites and games` → `Turn off`
Set `Game and app notifications` → `Turn off`

sources.label: Facebook Profile → Settings & privacy → Settings → Apps and websites

items.name: Switch to a private account
items.path: Instagram → Settings → Account privacy → Private account
items.why: A public Instagram account means your photos, location tags, tagged people, comments, and following list are visible to anyone on the internet - and indexed by search engines. Private accounts require approval before someone can follow you and see your content.

steps.text: Open Instagram → tap your profile icon → tap the hamburger menu → `Settings and privacy`
Tap `Account privacy`
Toggle on `Private account`
Review your existing followers and remove any you don't recognize: go to your profile → `Followers` → tap the three dots next to a follower → `Remove`

items.name: Hide activity status and read receipts
items.path: Instagram → Settings → Messages and story replies → Show activity status
items.why: Instagram shows other users when you were last active and whether you've read their messages. This gives stalkers, abusers, and anyone monitoring you a real-time signal of when you're using your phone.

steps.text: Go to `Settings and privacy` → `Messages and story replies`
Turn off `Show activity status`
Note: turning this off also means you won't see others' activity status

items.name: Opt out of data sharing with Meta partners
items.path: Instagram → Settings → Ads → Ad preferences
items.why: Instagram shares your activity with Meta's broader ad ecosystem, including information about posts you view, products you browse, and how long you spend on content. This feeds the same profile as Facebook's ad targeting.

steps.text: Go to `Settings and privacy` → `Ads` → `Ad preferences`
Under `Ad settings`, turn off `Ads based on data from partners`
Turn off `Ads based on your activity on Meta Products`
Also go to `accountscenter.facebook.com` → `Ad preferences` and apply the same settings - the accounts center manages both Facebook and Instagram together

items.name: Remove location data from posts and disable location access
items.path: Phone Settings → Instagram → Location
items.why: Location tags on photos reveal your home, workplace, and daily patterns over time. A history of tagged posts is a detailed map of your life. Photos also contain GPS metadata in the image file itself unless stripped.

steps.text: On iPhone: `Settings` → `Apps` → `Instagram` → `Location` → set to `Never` or `While using`
On Android: `Settings` → `Apps` → `Instagram` → `Permissions` → `Location` → set to `Denied` or `Only while using`
Before posting photos, don't add location tags - tap the location field and leave it blank
To remove location from past posts: go to the post → tap the three dots → `Edit` → tap the location tag → `Remove location`

items.name: Protect your posts (private account)
items.path: X → Settings → Privacy and safety → Audience and tagging
items.why: Public X/Twitter accounts are fully indexed by search engines. Every post, like, and reply is permanently public and searchable. Protected accounts limit your posts to approved followers only.

steps.text: Go to `Settings and support` → `Settings and privacy` → `Privacy and safety`
Under `Audience and tagging`, toggle on `Protect your posts`
Existing followers keep access - review your follower list and remove anyone you don't want reading your posts: `Profile` → `Followers` → three-dot menu next to any follower → `Remove follower`

items.name: Turn off discoverability by email and phone
items.path: X → Settings → Privacy and safety → Discoverability and contacts
items.why: By default, X allows anyone who has your phone number or email address to find your account. This lets people you've never connected with on X identify your account from a phone contact.

steps.text: Go to `Settings` → `Privacy and safety` → `Discoverability and contacts`
Turn off `Let people who have your email address find you on X`
Turn off `Let people who have your phone number find you on X`
Under `Contacts`, tap `Remove all contacts` to delete any previously synced phone contacts

items.name: Opt out of data sharing and personalization
items.path: X → Settings → Privacy and safety → Data sharing and personalization
items.why: X shares data with advertising partners and uses your activity - including off-platform browsing on sites with X buttons - to build an ad profile. Opting out limits how this data is used.

steps.text: Go to `Settings` → `Privacy and safety` → `Data sharing and personalization`
Turn off `Allow additional information sharing with business partners`
Under `Ads preferences`, turn off `Personalized ads`
Under `Off-X activity`, turn off `Allow use of where you see X content across the web`
Tap `See your X data` → `Interests and ads data` → review and remove interest categories X has assigned to you

items.name: Consider deleting TikTok entirely
items.path: TikTok → Profile → Settings → Manage account → Delete account
items.why: TikTok is owned by ByteDance, a Chinese company legally required to comply with Chinese national security laws that can compel data sharing with the Chinese government. Security researchers have documented that TikTok collects an extraordinary amount of device data - clipboard content, keystroke patterns, network information, and more - far beyond what its stated functionality requires.

steps.text: If you decide to keep TikTok, complete the settings below to reduce your exposure. Understand that core data collection happens at the platform level regardless of these settings
To delete: `Profile` → hamburger menu → `Settings and privacy` → `Manage account` → `Delete account`
Before deleting, request your data download: `Settings` → `Account` → `Download your data`

items.name: Set account to private
items.path: TikTok → Settings → Privacy → Private account
items.why: A public TikTok account means your videos, likes, following list, and profile are visible to anyone. Private accounts limit your content to approved followers.

steps.text: Go to `Profile` → hamburger menu → `Settings and privacy` → `Privacy`
Toggle on `Private account`
Under `Discoverability`, turn off `Suggest your account to others`

items.name: Revoke unnecessary device permissions
items.path: Phone Settings → TikTok → Permissions
items.why: TikTok requests access to contacts, location, microphone, camera, and other sensors. Most of this access is not needed for watching or creating videos. Revoking it limits how much the app can collect about your device and physical environment.

steps.text: On iPhone: `Settings` → `Apps` → `TikTok` → review each permission
On Android: `Settings` → `Apps` → `TikTok` → `Permissions`
Revoke: `Contacts`, `Location` (set to Never), `Microphone` (allow only while using if you make videos), `Calendar`, `Body sensors`
Leave Camera on only if you create content - set to Allow only while using

items.name: Opt out of targeted ads and personalization
items.path: TikTok → Settings → Privacy → Ads
items.why: TikTok uses your in-app behavior and off-platform data to serve targeted ads and build a behavioral profile. Opting out limits how this data is used for advertising.

steps.text: Go to `Settings and privacy` → `Privacy` → `Ads`
Turn off `Ad personalization`
Under `Data from partners`, turn off `Use of off-TikTok activity for ad targeting`

items.name: Control who can see your profile and activity
items.path: LinkedIn → Settings → Visibility → Visibility of your profile and network
items.why: LinkedIn profiles are public by default and indexed by search engines, meaning your full employment history, education, connections, and email address are visible to anyone. LinkedIn data is a primary source for targeted phishing attacks and social engineering.

steps.text: Go to `Settings & Privacy` → `Visibility` → `Visibility of your profile and network`
Set `Profile viewing options` to `Private mode` if you're browsing profiles and don't want to be seen
Set `Who can see or download your email address` to `1st-degree connections` or `Only you`
Turn off `Representing your organization and interests` to stop LinkedIn using your profile in ads
Set `Who can see your connections` to `Only you`

items.name: Opt out of data sharing with third parties
items.path: LinkedIn → Settings → Data privacy
items.why: LinkedIn shares profile data and activity with third-party partners including Microsoft's ad ecosystem. It also uses your profile for salary research, audience insight products sold to employers, and recruiter tools.

steps.text: Go to `Settings & Privacy` → `Data privacy`
Turn off `Data sharing with LinkedIn corporate affiliates` (Microsoft, Bing)
Under `Research invitations`, turn off `LinkedIn research`
Under `Salary data`, turn off `Contribute salary data`
Under `Social, economic, and workplace research`, turn off participation

items.name: Opt out of AI training on your content
items.path: LinkedIn → Settings → Data privacy → Data for AI improvement
items.why: LinkedIn uses your posts, comments, profile data, and activity to train Microsoft's AI models. This opt-out was added quietly in 2024 - most users are opted in by default.

steps.text: Go to `Settings & Privacy` → `Data privacy` → `Data for Generative AI Improvement`
Toggle off `Use my data for training content creation AI models`
Toggle off `Use my data for improving the relevance of ads`

items.name: Enable MFA on every social media account
items.path: Each platform → Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication
items.why: Social media account takeover is common and destructive - attackers use compromised accounts to spread misinformation, scam your followers, or publicly post content to damage your reputation. MFA makes this dramatically harder even if your password is leaked.

steps.text: Facebook: `Settings` → `Security and login` → `Two-factor authentication` → use an authenticator app
Instagram: `Settings` → `Accounts center` → `Password and Security` → `Two-factor authentication`
X: `Settings` → `Security and account access` → `Security` → `Two-factor authentication`
TikTok: `Profile` → `Settings` → `Security` → `2-step verification`
LinkedIn: `Settings` → `Sign in & security` → `Two-step verification`
On all platforms: choose authenticator app over SMS wherever possible - see the Passwords & MFA guide for setup instructions

items.name: Stop using social logins on other websites
items.path: Each platform → Settings → Apps and websites
items.why: Every time you use 'Continue with Facebook' or 'Sign in with Google' on a third-party website, you're connecting your social account to that service and telling the platform which services you use. Revoking old connections limits how your data flows between platforms.

steps.text: Facebook: `Settings` → `Security and login` → `Apps and websites` - remove any you no longer use
Instagram: `accountscenter.facebook.com` → `Your information and permissions` → `Apps and websites`
X: `Settings` → `Security and account access` → `Apps and sessions` → `Connected apps`
LinkedIn: `Settings` → `Data privacy` → `Other applications`
Going forward: create standalone accounts using a masked email rather than social login - see the phone masking guide for email relay options

items.name: Audit and remove tagged photos
items.path: Each platform → Profile → Photos
items.why: Photos others have tagged you in reveal your appearance, location, social connections, and activities - often without your knowledge or consent. Platforms use face recognition on tagged photos to build biometric profiles.

steps.text: Facebook: `Profile` → `Photos` → `Photos of you` - remove tags from any photos you don't want associated with your profile
Facebook: `Settings` → `Profile and tagging` → Turn off `Review posts you're tagged in before the post appears on your profile`... actually turn ON tag review so you approve tags before they appear
Instagram: `Profile` → hamburger menu → `Your activity` → `Photos and videos` → `Tagged posts` - remove unwanted tags
Instagram: `Settings` → `Privacy` → `Tags` → set `Allow tags from` to `People you follow`

items.name: Delete unused accounts
items.path: Account settings → Delete or deactivate account
items.why: Dormant accounts are liabilities. They contain years of data, are more likely to be forgotten and left unprotected, and continue to accumulate data even when you're not using them

steps.text: Before deleting: download your data archive from each platform - Facebook, Instagram, X, and TikTok all offer this in settings under 'Your information' or 'Download your data'
Facebook: `Settings` → `Your Facebook information` → `Deactivation and deletion`
Instagram: `accountscenter.facebook.com` → `Personal details` → `Account ownership and control` → `Deactivation or deletion`
X: `Settings` → `Your account` → `Deactivate account` (becomes permanent after 30 days)
TikTok: `Profile` → `Settings` → `Manage account` → `Delete account`

items.name: Avoid your account being tied to shared links
items.path: FINISH
items.why: When you share a Facebook or Instagram post on a different platform, your account is automatically tied to the shortened link. So if someone you're not connected to on Facebook clicks on that link, they will see a pop up to add you as a friend or to see your profile on Facebook. This is avoidable with a little bit of effort.

steps.text: Facebook: FINISH
